behavior_in_task_description.explanation: The instruction is deliberately vague: the video is meant to carry the defects. Still, its normative requirement is that every sprite-like element shows exactly what it was set up to show, at every moment, from every side, however it is placed, turned or carried. Every test is a direct consequence of that rule plus Luanti's documented entity API (spritediv/set_sprite animation, select_x_by_camera columns, texture orientation on front/back faces and on billboards). The tests ask for no file names, output formats or interfaces beyond fixing the rendering.

behavior_in_tests.explanation: There is a probe for each kind of element and case the instruction covers. Animated upright sprites and camera-facing sprites are checked, including frames driven by set_sprite. Attached ('carried') sprites of both kinds are checked. Texture orientation is checked on camera-facing sprites and on both the front and back of upright sprites ('from every side'). select_x_by_camera is checked at 4 yaws from two view axes ('however it is turned'). Pass-to-pass tests guard against over-correction.

informative_test_structure.explanation: run_test.py has a detailed module docstring, named constants for the sample boxes and palettes, and comments explaining the yaw conventions and expected columns. Each test id is descriptive (e.g. upright_sprite_back_is_not_mirrored), and failure messages give the observed vs expected colours. The Lua probe mod documents its scene layout. test.sh and verifier.py are clearly sectioned.

anti_cheating_measures.explanation: The bug patches are applied and deleted in the same RUN. Git history is replaced by a fresh harbor_base commit, so the fix commit cannot be reached, and file timestamps are normalised. Tests and the probe mod stay hidden until grading, and test.sh restores games/devtest and any paths the tests touch from harbor_base. The verifier rebuilds the real client and judges rendered pixels, so changing the Lua or server state cannot fake a pass. No network access is available to the agent.

structured_data_schema.explanation: The task is a source-code bug fix in a C++ engine; the agent produces no structured output.

pinned_dependencies.explanation: Only apt packages are installed (python3-pil included), and apt pinning is not required. The repository is fetched at a fixed base commit hash. No unpinned pip or npm dependencies are used.

typos.explanation: Paths are consistent across the instruction, Dockerfile, manifest and tests: /app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4, /app/bin/minetest, tests/harvest_c01/run_test.py, and the test ids in config.json, task.toml and run_test.py. test.sh has some leftover boilerplate comments about 'wx' and an unused REPORTS array, but neither changes behaviour. No typos that would cause a failure were found.

tests_or_solution_in_image.explanation: The Dockerfile copies only bugs/ (deleted in the same layer) and assets/recording.mp4. Neither tests/ nor solution/ is copied into the image.

test_deps_in_image.explanation: The image installs Xvfb, Mesa, ffmpeg and python3-pil. The instruction explicitly tells the agent to use ffmpeg to inspect the video, and Xvfb/Mesa let the agent build, run and reproduce the client, so these tools serve the agent as well as the tests. The test harness, probe mod and textures are added only at verification time through test.patch.

hardcoded_solution.explanation: solve.sh applies fix.patch, a real source-code change across CBillboardSceneNode.cpp, content_cao.cpp, mesh.cpp and mesh.h. It reverses each injected defect and marks the vertex buffer dirty. It does not echo any answer.

file_reference_mentioned.explanation: The agent fixes source code in place and does not need to produce any output files.
